messages:
Anya P: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands — can we get a concise clarification on the microbatching rollout timeline and expected p50/p95 impacts? I'm compiling a short note for PMs.
Devin R: Short answer: microbatching targeted for next sprint (2 weeks) behind canary. p50 should improve ~8-12% on text-gen workloads; p95 may vary up to ~20% depending on KV cache hit rate. We'll post detailed perf numbers by EOD tomorrow.
Tony L: +1. Note that kernel v4 attention-fusing changes are blocking one quantized execution path. Plan is a fallback to keep latency stable for Dedicated customers.
Cecilia (Eng lead): To add: canary will run in us-west-2 first, then eu-west. Ops will run the perf harness against 4 representative prompts. @ops-bot can you create a perf job and tag results?
ops-bot: Created job perf/microbatch-canary-289123. Results will be added to the dashboard: https://console.redwood/perf/jobs/289123
Anya P: Thanks — two quick follow-ups: 1) will cache prewarm be required for the canary? 2) Any client-facing config changes (e.g., exposing batch_window_ms)?
Devin R: 1) We plan optional prewarm for high-latency models; default canary won't require prewarm. 2) We may expose batch_window_ms for alpha customers; default stays 10ms. We'll add an example config in the docs.
Tony L: For kernel team: FYI if model length distribution skews longer, microbatching can increase p95. Recommend ticket: "adaptive-batch-window-by-seqlen" so the runtime can shrink/expand windows. @Cecilia can you triage?
Cecilia (Eng lead): Created ticket RNW-1227 and assigned to Lev S. Lev, can you estimate effort?
Lev S: I'll take this today. Quick estimate: 3-5 days to prototype an adaptive window + 2 days for perf runs and validation. Primary risk: regressions on very short-seq, small-batch workloads.
Devin R: Example config snippet we might document for alpha customers:
```json
{"batch_window_ms": 10, "enable_microbatch": true}
```
Anya P: Perfect. Last ask — Product wants a short blurb for release notes highlighting expected improvements, possible regressions, and the config knobs. Who can draft?
Devin R: I can draft the blurb and open a PR against the docs by EOD tomorrow.
Tony L: Also, if any Dedicated customer reports regressions, route to support@redwood.com and we will escalate with an emergency canary rollback option.
Cecilia (Eng lead): Thanks all — I'll post consolidated follow-up notes in the all-hands doc once we have perf numbers and the perf job link.
